heading: ## The first turn
goal: Goal: the person plays the game the brief describes on the Stage, made as well as you can make it: every part a player sees is yours to design.
read: Read `BRIEF.md` and the bridge contract in `TEMPLATE.md` (what the harness needs from the game, nothing about how it looks), then build the game in `web/`. Write no plan or design document.
watched: The person watches the Stage while you work: it shows the game from the first frame it draws and follows every save. Get a scene they can see running first, then grow the game in place.

made.blender: made in Blender (each Blender tool names its recipe), after the whole game plays with quick models in code standing in, one at a time, each replacing its stand-in once it looks better in the game
made.generated: generated from the key art below by the person's providers, with quick models in code standing in until they arrive
made.code: built in three.js code, never bare primitives standing in for them

library: The person turned the asset library on: use its models where it has what the brief names (`game_assets` op `search`; the first `add` takes `lock`), and the rest are {made}.
chosen: The person chose how the game's models are made: its player, main threat and world are {made}.
blenderRoute: The person chose how the game's models are made, by kind: the player, its characters and its creatures are made in Blender (each Blender tool names its recipe); so are trees, rocks and buildings and the prop the game is about; the rest is built in three.js code. Build the whole game first with quick models in code standing in, so the person plays it, then make the Blender models one at a time, each replacing its stand-in once it looks better than the stand-in in the game. If `game_check` op `status` shows no Blender, build the characters in code too and tell the person that Settings → Game tools takes a Blender.
generated: Start the key art first: `game_assets` op `generate` with lane `image`, name `key_art`, `options.aspect` `"16:9"`, a prompt holding the game's world and moment in one image, and three `directions`: looks that truly differ, each one this game can reach, each grounded with a `style` (a library pack id that ships a picture of its look, or the person's own reference image; `studio-skills/art-pipeline.md`, Generated art). It renders while you build; never wait on it, and if it is refused, say so and go on. Before you end the turn, op `wait` for it: ask the person to pick one of its candidates in the chat, or say it is still rendering, and say what it cost.
reference: The person attached a picture to aim for, attached here and saved as `art/reference.png`. When it holds more than the one view you will match (a phone screenshot, a page around it), save that view alone over it. The model sheet and the check show it beside yours.
